name: Behind the Behaviour
headline: Every behaviour. Is a message.
intro: Training that helps your team read what a behaviour is telling them and stay calm through the hardest moments.
glance: 6 hours in person, or 2 hours live online

problem.scene: A child swears and walks out of class.
problem.question: Is it defiance, or a message?
without: The adult reads it as defiance
with: Staff read the reason behind it
Records say what happened and what helped
problem.standards: The DfE's 2026 guidance on restrictive interventions in schools and the Children's Homes (England) Regulations 2015 both expect prevention and de-escalation first. This course shows staff how.
problem.evidence: It is not physical intervention training. If staff need restraint techniques, they come from a specialist provider, and this course sits alongside that.

groups: Teachers, teaching assistants, pastoral leads, SENCOs and designated teachers
Staff, managers and supported accommodation teams
Foster carers, kinship carers and supervising social workers
Early help and family support workers
notes: Staff from different roles can train together

outcomes: See it from the child's side
Describe a refusal or outburst from the child's side: what they felt, needed and heard.
Recognise when a child is moving out of their window of tolerance, and the triggers in your setting.
Use Siegel's window of tolerance and Bowlby's attachment theory to explain how trauma shapes behaviour.
Know your setting's rules on restraint
Explain Regulate, Relate, Reason, and what your setting's rules require before any restrictive intervention.
Use PACE and Spot, Soothe, Shift to bring a tense moment down without ultimatums.
Plan a repair conversation and write an incident record that is factual and free of labels.

pillars.title: Regulate, Relate, Reason
pillars.stance_line: A child has to feel calm before they can connect, and connect before they can think it through.
items: Help the child feel calm and safe first. One adult, fewer words, a calm voice.
Connect with the child. PACE keeps the adult alongside them while the moment passes.
Only then think it through together, and repair what happened.
pillars.base: Bruce Perry's Regulate, Relate, Reason, with Dan Siegel's window of tolerance and Dan Hughes's PACE.

story_line: Three stories run through the day: Jade, 13, at school; Kai, 14, in a new home; and Mason, 9, at his foster home. Each is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on trauma-informed practice, including Middlesbrough's town-wide programme to make every school attachment aware and trauma informed, and Durham's children's homes, where he trained 120 residential staff.
He led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education, so he knows what the standards expect of the adults around a child.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
